subject: Cross-border controls & standby region playbook for private VPC deployments
body:
From: Sophie Moreau <sophie.moreau@euro-retail.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:12:00 +0200
Subject: Request: standby-region controls for EU primary, APAC failover

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — EuroRetail is keen to proceed with a private VPC deployment where EU remains primary by policy, but APAC must be available as a cold/standby region in the event of a datacentre outage or regulatory requirement.

Two asks to start the conversation:
- A concise checklist of controls we need to demonstrate for EU-first data residency (networking, KMS key residency, audit logs, and data-at-rest handling).
- A failover playbook outline for an APAC standby region (what data moves, how long failover takes, what we keep local, and how DNS/routing and customer traffic would be handled).

We have internal auditors looking for sloppy cross-border movement to be avoided unless explicitly approved; they also want to see a timeline for any data replication and cryptographic key handling.

Can your team produce a short playbook + recommended configuration for our infra architects and security reviewers?

Best,
Sophie Moreau
Head of Cloud Architecture | EuroRetail GmbH
---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Team — forwarding Sophie's ask from EuroRetail. High priority customer; compliance team will require clear artifacts. Please see the two bullets above.

Marcus: can you draft the network/design portion (VPC peering, egress controls, private endpoints, cross-region replication policy)?
Mina: please prepare the compliance checklist for EU residency and outline what evidence we can provide (KMS region binding, audit log retention, data classification).
Rishi: estimate the costs and practical RTO for a cold standby (snapshot replication vs streaming replication), and note any limits we should be upfront about.

Deliverable target: short playbook + network diagram + an attachments package by end of day Aug 12. I'll package and send to Sophie with our recommended controls and a proposed PoC timeline.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: standby-region controls for EU primary, APAC failover

Laura / team —

High-level network/design notes (draft):

1) Network topology (attached: network-diagram-v2.png)
   - EU primary lives in customer-controlled VPC in eu-central-1, with private subnets for inference nodes and a restricted management plane subnet for the control plane.
   - APAC standby provisioned in ap-northeast-1 as an isolated VPC with identical subnets, but all external egress disabled until activated.
   - Cross-region connectivity uses encrypted transit (TLS + IPSec) but only for snapshot metadata and manifest replication; full KV/cache state is not replicated proactively.

2) Data movement policy
   - Snapshots of model weights and customer-configured prompts (non-sensitive metadata) can be replicated as encrypted artifacts to the APAC standby S3 bucket with the customer's explicit consent and documented approval.
   - Customer PII / regulated tokens are never replicated to standby by default. If customer requests replication, require documented justification, KMS key located in APAC with dual-control approval, and an SLA amendment.

3) DNS & routing failover
   - Route53 / global DNS with health-check-based failover: primary EU endpoints in the global record with weighted 100 -> 0 to standby. On failover, we shift weights to APAC and update edge routing.
   - For lower RTO, use anycast + control-plane routing to bring APAC inference pools online pre-warmed via cached images (cost tradeoff).

4) Security controls (network)
   - Private endpoints for control plane; no public control-plane egress.
   - Strict security groups and NACLs enforcing minimal ports.
   - Audit-only logs shipped to EU-retained logging bucket; replication to APAC is disabled unless customer signs off.

I'll attach a PNG network diagram and a short checklist. Need Mina to confirm KMS / audit statements for the compliance artifact.

— Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: network-diagram-v2.png

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:30:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: standby-region controls for EU primary, APAC failover

Adding compliance checklist (high level):

- Data residency controls (EU primary)
  * KMS keys: customer-managed keys (CMKs) created in eu-central-1; by default, KMS policy denies cross-region decrypt.
  * Audit logs: S3 bucket in EU for audit-logs with versioning + MFA delete enabled. Retention policy configurable to meet local regs.
  * Access controls: RBAC enforced via IAM + session policies limited to EU console endpoints for auditors.

- Replication & approvals
  * Replication windows: snapshots are asynchronous. Documented approval required for any snapshot copying to APAC.
  * Dual-control process: change requests that enable cross-region replication require 2 approvers (customer sec + Redwood CISO delegate).

- Evidence artifacts we can provide
  * Signed KMS policy export (region binding statement)
  * Audit log samples (redacted) showing access from EU-only addresses for the period requested
  * Signed change record for any cross-region replication event

I'll export the sample policies and a template change request (SOP) to attach.

— Mina
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-standby-region-checklist.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 07:45:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: standby-region controls for EU primary, APAC failover

Quick cost and RTO notes:
- Cold standby (snapshot-only, no warm instances): minimal monthly cost for storage replication manifest and object storage in APAC (~estimated EUR 1k/mo for EuroRetail scale). RTO: 4–8 hours (provisioning + state restore).
- Warm standby (pre-provisioned instance pool, no live replication): higher cost (approx EUR 6–8k/mo), RTO: 15–30 mins for DNS cutover and activation.
- Full active-active with geo-replication: significant architecture changes (data partitioning, cross-region KMS policies), not recommended unless business requires sub-second continuity.

Notes: need to sign off whether model KV caches can be discarded on failover (recommended) vs synchronous replication (costly and risky for residency).

— Rishi
Head of Product Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachment: cs-proof-of-concept-notes.pdf

Subject: RE: Request: standby-region controls for EU primary, APAC failover

Hi Sophie / Kenji —

Thanks for the clear ask. Please find attached: network-diagram-v2.png, SLA-standby-region-checklist.xlsx, and a short PoC notes PDF. Key points and recommendation summary: 

Summary recommendations
- Default posture: EU primary only; no automatic replication of PII or customer-sensitive config to APAC.
- Standby model: cold standby via encrypted snapshot replication (customer opt-in). This gives a good balance of cost and compliance; expected RTO 4–8 hours.
- Failover flow: documented SOP with DNS weight shift, pre-approved change request, and temporary KMS key delegation (APAC) only if customer approves.
- Evidence: we can provide KMS policy exports, redacted audit log slices, and the signed change record for any replica event.

Next steps
1) Sophie: please confirm whether EuroRetail is open to snapshot-only standby (opt-in) or requires warm standby.
2) If opt-in, sign the attached change-request template and we will schedule a 2-week PoC (network + compliance evidence collection).
3) We will provide a short runbook for your infra team covering DNS, routing, and the exact activation checklist.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync to walk through the attachments; Marcus and Mina will join to answer network/compliance questions.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
Attachments: network-diagram-v2.png, SLA-standby-region-checklist.xlsx, cs-proof-of-concept-notes.pdf
